title: The lands were gone, but the life was mine
era: 1995 World Championship-era Standard illustration using modern timing
matchup: Rack Control against white land-destruction control
story: My opponent cast Armageddon , and I had Zuran Orb on the battlefield with a Plains and Swamp still untapped. Before Armageddon resolved, I sacrificed both lands to Orb in separate activations. I gained two life from each ability, taking my total from six to ten. The sacrificed lands had already gone to the graveyard; Armageddon could not destroy them a second time. I kept The Rack in play, but I had also surrendered both mana sources. Orb did not tap, and none of that life arrived because I had paid mana to activate it.
review: Armageddon on stack, Orb sacrifice of Plains/Swamp as two separate costs, 2+2 lifegain from 6->10 before Armageddon. Lands gone before sweep, Orb stays. Opponent invented, named deck contains Orb/Rack/lands.
claim: representative reconstruction; not a historical match or quotation
